pages.description: Encyclopedia article on the Scotch Malt Whisky Society.
pages.text:
The Scotch Malt Whisky Society Ltd.
Founded: 1983
Founder: Phillip Hills
Headquarters: Edinburgh, Scotland, UK
Owner: The Artisanal Spirits Company plc

The Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS) is a membership organisation based in Edinburgh. It bottles single malt whisky from Scotland and elsewhere and sells it directly to its members. It runs four members' rooms in the United Kingdom, and has branches in more than 20 other countries.

History
The Society began with Phillip "Pip" Hills, who tasted whisky drawn straight from the cask on trips around the Highlands in the late 1970s. In 1978 he persuaded some acquaintances to share the cost of a cask from the Glenfarclas distillery. The group grew into a small syndicate that bought more casks and shared the bottles among its subscribers.

In 1983 the Society opened membership to the public and bought its first property, The Vaults in Leith, whose wine cellars are said to date back to the 12th century. It set up members' rooms there.

In 1996 the Society started a share scheme for members and used the money to buy a venue in London.

In 2004 the Society opened a second Edinburgh venue, a Georgian townhouse on Queen Street. In the same year, the Society was acquired by Glenmorangie plc.

For its 25th anniversary the Society redesigned its bottles, adding more information and a full tasting note to the front.

In 2010 the Society worked with the Hotel du Vin and Malmaison hotel chains to add 'whisky snug' bars to their hotels.

In 2015, Glenmorangie plc, by then owned by LVMH, sold the Society to private investors.

In June 2021 the private owners listed the holding company, The Artisanal Spirits Company plc, on the Alternative Investment Market of the London Stock Exchange.

Bottlings
A tasting panel approves each cask before the Society buys it. Each bottling has a two-part code: the first number is the distillery and the second is the cask, so 2.35 is the 35th cask from distillery number two. Most bottlings are at cask strength, often above 55% ABV. By September 2010 the Society had bottled about 3,597 single casks since 1983.

pages.text:
The Scotch Malt Whisky Society. Independent bottler. Private members' club and independent bottler of whiskies and spirits.

Profile
The Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS) is a private members' club and one of the oldest of Scotland's modern independent bottlers. It helped popularise single cask whisky bottled at cask strength. Its bottles share one presentation and are named by a numbered code. Besides whisky it has bottled Cognac, Armagnac, rum, Bourbon and Somerset cider brandy. Its bottlings are sold to members only.

History
The SMWS was founded in 1983 by a group of friends including tax accountant Philip 'Pip' Hills, actor Russell Hunter, contractor David Alison, writer W Gordon Smith and architect Ben Tindall.

The friends had bought a cask of Glenfarclas and drew bottles from it to share. In 1983 part of the Vaults buildings in Leith became free when the previous occupant, J G Thomson, moved to Glasgow.

A membership society was set up, and the friends' cask of Glenfarclas, a 1975 sherry cask, was released as the first SMWS bottling, labelled 1.1, in August 1983. New bottlings followed each month.

In 1995 Hills resigned as a director, and the company carried on without him. The next year the SMWS offered its members a share scheme and used the money to buy a second members' club, on Greville Street in London.

In 2004 the SMWS opened its third venue at 28 Queen Street in Edinburgh, and was sold later the same year to Glenmorangie.

In 2008, for its 25th anniversary, the SMWS changed its bottle shape and added a longer tasting note to the label. The bottles changed again in 2017 to show the whisky styles more clearly.

The SMWS was sold to a private consortium of investors in 2015.

pages.title: Scotch Malt Whisky Society Under New Ownership - WhiskyCast
pages.description: News report on the 2015 sale of the Scotch Malt Whisky Society.
pages.text:
Scotch Malt Whisky Society Under New Ownership

March 31, 2015 - The Glenmorangie Company has sold the Scotch Malt Whisky Society to a group of investors led by the Society's current executives, for an undisclosed sum.

The Society was founded in 1984 and has owned and franchised chapters in 19 countries, with more than 25,000 members. It is one of the largest independent bottlers of Scotch whisky and releases about 350 single cask bottlings to its members each year. The sale includes the members' rooms at The Vaults in Leith, in Edinburgh, and in London.

Managing director Paul Miles said more than half of the ownership will be in Scottish hands and that the whole management team is part of the investor group, with a small amount of international investment. The United States is the Society's biggest growth market, followed by Taiwan, Japan and China.

Glenmorangie's president and CEO, Marc Hoellinger, said the sale lets the company focus on its Glenmorangie and Ardbeg single malts. The LVMH-owned company has sold other distilleries and most of its blended Scotch business in recent years. Glenmorangie acquired the SMWS in 2004.

pages.title: SMWS prohibits non-member purchases | Scotch Whisky
pages.description: News report on the Scotch Malt Whisky Society ending sales to non-members.
pages.text:
SMWS prohibits non-member purchases
27 September 2017 by Becky Paskin

Bottles released by the Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS) are no longer available to non-members, after feedback from members.

The society had offered a 'sample subscriber' option that let non-members buy bottlings at a 30% premium. To keep its bottlings exclusive, the SMWS withdrew that option on 26 September, after its largest survey of members that summer.

The change follows a range makeover, a new rare whisky series, and single cask rum, gin and Cognac in recent months.

Non-members can still buy gift memberships and tasting glasses. Kaleidoscope at Devonshire Square in London and 28 Queen Street in Edinburgh, which non-members may visit, will sell bottles only after a period when they are reserved for members.

Basic annual membership costs from £61.50.

The SMWS was founded in Leith in 1983, and today operates member clubs in 17 countries.

expected.notes: opened 1983: Wikipedia (Founded: 1983, and membership opened to the public with The Vaults bought in 1983), Whiskypedia (founded in 1983) and the 2017 news report (founded in Leith in 1983). acquired 2004: Glenmorangie, from Wikipedia (acquired by Glenmorangie plc), Whiskypedia (sold later the same year to Glenmorangie) and WhiskyCast (Glenmorangie acquired the SMWS in 2004). acquired 2015: private investors led by the Society's executives, from Wikipedia, Whiskypedia and WhiskyCast (dated March 31, 2015). Expected dates are year-level, so 2015-03-31 also passes.

notes: This is a bottler case: events are about the business, not single bottlings. Traps for the founding: the 1978 Glenfarclas cask shared by Hills and friends is the Society's origin, not its founding; WhiskyCast says founded in 1984, but the reference pages and the 2017 report say 1983, so an opened date of 1984 is wrong. The first bottling, cask 1.1 from a 1975 sherry cask in August 1983, is a bottling detail; 1975 is not an event year. The 12th-century cellars of The Vaults are not an event. LVMH owned Glenmorangie, not the Society, so LVMH is never the new owner. The June 2021 AIM listing was by the same private owners, so it is not an acquired event; it may be a generic event. Optional events: the 1995 resignation of Hills, the 1996 share scheme and London venue, the 2004 Queen Street venue, the 2008 bottle redesign, the 2010 hotel bars, the 2017 bottle redesign, the 2017 end of non-member sales and the 2021 listing. Noise to leave out: member counts, country counts, cask counts, ABV, bottle names and the membership price. Peated stores the Society as a bottler with owner The Artisanal Spirits Company, location Scotland and smws.com as website. Page texts are reviewed paraphrases of the cited pages, not copies.
